title: What Cloudflare Doubters Overlooked
detail:
What Cloudflare Doubters Overlooked
Bailey Pemberton
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 10:13 AM EST 4 min read
NET
Trade NET on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Cloudflare has given investors plenty to argue about this year, from a sector-wide sell off tied to AI worries to later headlines about AI agents, security certifications, and new business models. Investors who held Cloudflare from the start of the year are up 35.3%, including dividends. If you were deciding on 1 January whether to buy, how much weight would you have put on rich valuation versus the early AI and security story already on the table?

The useful thing about a Narrative is that the reasoning is checkable: the assumptions sit beside the argument, and together they imply an estimated Fair Value you can disagree with.

The move put Cloudflare in the middle of this trade. Scan 53 AI infrastructure stocks for other companies exposed to it.

The Two Cloudflare Stories Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost US$197 at the start, which meant any decision on Cloudflare hinged on which future investors believed in more.

The bullish narrative put fair value at US$209, 6% above the start price. It was built on an assumption of 26.5% annual revenue growth and profit margins rising to 4.6% within three years.

The bearish case pointed to fair value of US$116, 41% below the start price. It warned that rising cybersecurity regulation and hyperscaler pressure could erode margins even if revenue grew 24.8% a year.

NYSE:NET Trailing 12-Month Earnings & Revenue History as at Nov 2026
What The Cloudflare Evidence Actually Tested

Cloudflare's Q2 2026 update showed revenue at US$696.1 million versus US$512.3 million a year earlier, which backed the growth part of the bullish story. Profit went the other way. The firm reported a larger net loss and net margin moved from -9.8% to -24.4%, so the earlier profitability assumptions stayed unproven. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The key lesson is simple. When a bullish case leans on margin improvement, you need to track net margin, not just revenue. For any high-growth stock, compare the original margin pathway with each new earnings report and factor in whether that shift is actually turning up in the numbers.

What Cloudflare's Price Already Assumes Today

Cloudflare now trades at US$265, up strongly from US$197 from the start of the year, so any fresh decision leans heavily on what that quote already implies.

The selected Narrative's Fair Value sits below the current price and leans on Cloudflare as a post-quantum security layer rather than a pure quantum winner. A buyer today is effectively assuming that quantum era trust and security demand will justify this price. How does the Narrative's caution on standalone post-quantum revenue factor into that bet?

Key Takeaways

Cloudflare (NET) stock gained approximately 35% in 2026 through November 2, despite falling 28% from its October high as investors reassessed expensive AI and software stocks.

Datadog (DDOG) has also faced selling pressure, with its November 4 earnings report offering an early indication of enterprise cloud demand before Cloudflare reports on November 5.

Cloudflare's second-quarter revenue increased 36% to $696 million, while management raised its full-year revenue guidance to between $2.864 billion and $2.870 billion.

Cloudflare's expanding AI opportunities support its long-term growth outlook, but declining gross margins and a premium valuation make the stock a hold ahead of earnings.

What Happened?

Cloudflare (NET) stock gained approximately 35% in 2026 through November 2, climbing from $197 at the end of 2025 to $265, according to historical closing prices.

However, shares have fallen approximately 28% from their October 6 intraday high of $370 as investors grew increasingly cautious about richly valued AI infrastructure and software companies.

Datadog (DDOG) experienced similar sector pressure, making its November 4 earnings report an important indicator of enterprise cloud demand before Cloudflare reports on November 5.

Cloudflare's underlying business has continued expanding despite the stock's volatility.

First-quarter revenue increased 34% year over year to $639.8 million, exceeding management's guidance. However, non-GAAP gross margin declined to 72.8% from 74.9% in the previous quarter.

The company also announced plans to reduce its workforce by approximately 1,100 employees as it reorganized around AI and automation.

Shares fell approximately 24% on May 8 as investors weighed strong revenue growth against margin pressure and restructuring concerns.

Second-quarter results demonstrated continued momentum, with revenue increasing 36% to $696.1 million.

Management also raised its full-year revenue guidance to between $2.864 billion and $2.870 billion.

CEO Matthew Prince described the company's expanding opportunity in AI-driven Internet traffic, saying: "we are seeing a fundamental rewrite of the Internet for machine-to-machine traffic."

Cloudflare's developer ecosystem has expanded to more than 10 million developers, compared with 7.4 million at the end of the second quarter.

Its infrastructure for AI agents could create new revenue opportunities as websites begin charging automated systems for accessing content.

Meanwhile, Datadog's second-quarter revenue increased 36% to $1.12 billion, while customers generating more than $100,000 in annual recurring revenue increased 23% to approximately 4,720.

Key Takeaways

Zscaler fell 14% in the past week as reports from Fortinet and Check Point and a tech selloff hit security stocks, Cloudflare among them.

Fortinet beat estimates and still sank as its service revenue slowed, so Zscaler's late-November report will likely need more than a beat.

At a forward P/E well under its own history, Zscaler is a buy if those results run ahead of the guide.

Zscaler (ZS:NASDAQ) is down 14% in the week through the Nov. 2 close, giving back most of its PHP-flaw rally with no news of its own.

The selling started at Fortinet (FTNT:NASDAQ), spread as tech sold off, and picked up again when Check Point Software (CHKP:NASDAQ) reported on Nov. 2. Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) fell 20% over the same week.

Fortinet sank, and the security group went with it

Fortinet beat estimates after the Oct. 28 close and raised its 2026 revenue and billings outlook, and product revenue jumped 37%. But service revenue grew just 13%, and Fortinet cut its full-year service forecast to $5.15 billion to $5.17 billion, from $5.18 billion to $5.22 billion. The stock closed down 20.1% on Oct. 29, and Zscaler fell about 3% with it.

Fortinet blamed the slowdown on the timing of large new deals, but investors sold subscription names anyway. Zscaler leans on subscriptions even more: about 98% of its fiscal 2026 revenue came from subscriptions, and it expects growth to slow to 16.6% to 17.5% in fiscal 2027, from 25%.

Then tech and Check Point piled on

Tech sold off on Oct. 30 after disappointing results from Amazon and Intel, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.86%, its worst day since June 5. Zscaler lost 4.0% and Cloudflare 9.5%.

On Nov. 2, as tech kept falling, Check Point fell 6.98% after third-quarter revenue slipped 1.1% and missed estimates. Zscaler dropped 5.9%, and Cloudflare fell 5.5% after Jefferies cut its price target.

Cloudflare had rallied as website operators rushed to patch the PHP flaws, and it reports third-quarter results after the close on Nov. 5. Will that rush to patch show up in its numbers?

The first-quarter report faces a higher bar

At its Oct. 6 Investor Day, Zscaler stood by its fiscal 2027 outlook and laid out a base case for ARR above $8 billion by fiscal 2031. Neither has changed.

Consensus has revenue compounding at about 17% a year through fiscal 2029, with the fiscal 2027 estimate of $3.93 billion near the top of the $3.91 billion to $3.94 billion guide:

Zscaler (ZS): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024-2029 (years to July) (TIKR)

Nothing Zscaler did this week should move those estimates.

First-quarter results are due in late November, on revenue guidance of $935 million to $939 million. After Fortinet, the stock likely needs more than a beat: net new ARR ahead of plan, or a raised full-year outlook.

The catalyst that sent the edge computing and cybersecurity specialist lower was a bearish note from a Wall Street analyst.

Image source: Getty Images.

Great expectations

Jefferies analyst Joe Gallo maintained a hold rating on Cloudflare but lowered his price target to $320, down from $350. That still represents potential upside of 14% compared to Friday's closing price. The analyst suggests he expects higher demand for the company's cloud services in the current quarter but believes the bar may be set too high.

Analysts' consensus estimates call for revenue of $739 million, representing year-over-year growth of 32%, and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.34, up 26%. For context, Cloudflare's forecast calls for revenue in a range of $736 million and $737 million and adjusted EPS of $0.34, so Wall Street is predicting higher sales growth than management's outlook.

That's no coincidence. Cloudflare has an impressive track record of beating expectations, surpassing Wall Street's consensus estimates in each of the past four quarters. That said, investors are fickle, so there's no way to know for sure how the stock will react to any given quarter of financial results. We'll know for sure when Cloudflare reports after the market close on Thursday.

Taking a step back, however, suggests the future is bright. Just last month, Cloudflare deployed protective measures against the highly publicized PHP website vulnerability ahead of the public disclosure. PHP is used by roughly 70% of all websites, and this security vulnerability could have allowed hackers to access servers, steal customer data, and disrupt services, according to Cloudflare. Reports suggest there were thousands of hacking attempts leading up to the revelation and millions thereafter.

This helps to illustrate the importance of Cloudflare's cloud and cybersecurity services and why investors should focus beyond the company's next financial report.

Cloudflare's Q3 Outlook

Cloudflare's strong operating momentum provides a favorable foundation for continued growth in the third quarter and beyond. The company is positioned to benefit from sustained customer acquisition and expanding spending from its existing customer base. These factors are expected to support revenue growth.

www.barchart.com

Customer acquisition trends remain encouraging. During Q2, Cloudflare recorded its strongest pace of new customer bookings in more than five years, while new pipeline generation continued to accelerate, reaching its fastest sequential growth rate over the same period. NET added more than 80,000 paying customers during the quarter, up 74% year-over-year (YoY). This acceleration in customer additions highlights the continued demand for Cloudflare's platform and its ability to attract new users.

Equally important, Cloudflare is expanding its relationships with larger enterprise customers. At the end of Q2, the company had 4,698 customers generating more than $100,000 in annualized revenue, representing 27% YoY growth, compared with 25% in the previous quarter. Cloudflare added 282 large customers during Q2 and a record 986 over the past year. Notably, every enterprise spending cohort, ranging from $100,000 to $500,000, $1 million, and $5 million in annualized revenue, recorded its highest-ever YoY net customer additions. This broad-based expansion suggests that demand is strengthening across multiple enterprise spending tiers.

The growth in enterprise relationships is also reflected in Cloudflare's remaining performance obligations (RPO). Total RPO reached $2.73 billion, up 7% sequentially and 38% YoY. Meanwhile, the current RPO, which represents the portion expected to be recognized over the next 12 months, accounted for 64% of total RPO and increased 35% from the prior-year period. The sustained expansion in these metrics indicates a healthy backlog.
